candidates.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: production transparent action sprite atlas for a 2.5D RPG. Create a landscape 1536 x 1024 RGBA image containing exactly six independently drawn full-body sprites of the SAME brown-haired young male armored axe warrior CH01 as the three supplied reference images. The references are identity/costume/style guides, not layout or pose guides. Preserve his exact youthful face, tousled medium brown hair, charcoal plate armor with rich gold edging and star emblems, orange-red scarf, orange-red waist cloth, leather belt, armored boots and broad single-headed silver-edged charcoal-and-gold axe. Same detailed painterly storybook game-art style, crisp contours.

LAYOUT: invisible regular 3 columns x 2 rows, each cell 512 x 512. Clear transparent gutters. Each complete sprite, both feet, full axe and scarf fit inside its own cell with at least 15 pixels of transparent margin. No sprite overlaps another cell. Anatomical head crown to bottom of feet height should be 355-390 pixels in EVERY cell, excluding raised weapon; do not draw small figures. Consistent camera elevation about 25 degrees, feet fixed on ground, upright screen vertical bodies. No grid, labels, text, background, floor, shadows, magic, motion arcs or particles. Actual alpha transparency.

COLUMNS left to right: WINDUP, RELEASE / CONTACT, RECOVERY. Every column is a genuinely distinct pose showing a coherent two-handed axe attack.
TOP ROW: direction S, straight toward viewer and screen bottom. Torso, face, hips and boots face directly toward camera, bilaterally frontal. Windup lifts the axe overhead centered above his head using two hands. Release is a foreshortened forceful downward chop straight toward screen bottom: both hands extend forward at abdomen height and the axe haft projects toward viewer, its blade/contact edge BELOW both hands centered on his body axis, not to either side; foreshortening must read as a real forward/down-screen strike. Recovery brings the axe down and in at center with bent knees, maintaining frontal S orientation.
BOTTOM ROW: direction SE, toward viewer and screen lower-right at a true 45-degree angle. Full torso, face, hips and boots turned toward lower-right. Windup lifts the axe over rear shoulder. Release is a two-handed diagonal chop with the axe blade clearly projecting lower-right of both hands. Recovery follows through low toward lower-right. Not merely the frontal row with head turned: all three are separately drawn 3/4 view poses.

Keep anatomy complete and coherent. No whole-body rotation, no mirrored reused frames, no detached weapons, no extra arms or axes, no cropped feet. Strongly preserve reference warrior and his armor details. Prioritize genuine S and SE directional axe contact geometry.
candidates.review: All six independent silhouettes complete, direction S is frontal axe below hands, SE is lower-right. Nonuniform observed regions avoid unrelated sprites. Initial raw-RGB/background and fixed-grid concerns resolved by alpha/component inspection; no image edit needed.

Recovery retains actual visible weapon geometry, which may differ from release direction.
